title: Rabbi Taddai
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman cites Shabbat 35b for a teaching Rabbi Abba reports in the name of Rabbi Taddai. In [Shabbat 38b:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.38b.2), Rabbi Zerika transmits it from Rabbi Abba in Rabbi Taddai’s name.
At [Shabbat 38b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.38b.2), Rabbi Ami says that Rabbi Taddai acted on his own authority.
In Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 6:8: Rabbi Simon, Rabbi Taddai in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua [ben Levi].

In Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 3:1: Rabbi Simon deTarei; the reading of Yuchasin HaShalem is Rabbi Simon bar Taddai. Hyman considers it undoubtedly originally written “b״r,” meaning “in the name of Rabbi Taddai.” There is also Rabbi Elazar ben Taddai. Hyman cites Shabbat 123b; the named ruling is at [Shabbat 123a:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.123a.9).[^3]
Rabbi Yose ben Taddai: Derekh Eretz Rabbah, beginning of chapter 1.

notes.text: The consulted Shabbat 38b contains both Rabbi Abba’s transmission from Rabbi Taddai and Rabbi Ami’s remark. Hyman places the first at 35b. His locator and proposed Yuchasin abbreviation reconstruction are preserved; no printed-page verification is claimed.

The consulted Shabbat 35b does not show this chain. At [Shabbat 38b:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.38b.2), Rabbi Zerika cites Rabbi Abba in Rabbi Taddai’s name, and Rabbi Ami then comments on Taddai’s practice. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3535&lang=en) cites both statements at 38b.
The linked Shabbat 123a ruling names Rabbi Elazar ben Taddai, and Rav Nachman follows his opinion. The attribution in Shabbat 38b concerns Rabbi Taddai himself.
